messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The reported issue is that Base64InputStream.read(byte[]) incorrectly returns 0 at the end of any stream whose length is a multiple of 3 bytes. This causes problems when wrapping Base64InputStream with InputStreamReader, which fails if read(byte[]) returns 0 prematurely.

The key method to inspect is Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int), which is implemented with a loop to handle the case where the underlying Base64 decoding returns 0 bytes read by retrying. The code comment there explicitly notes this is a workaround for streams with lots of non-base64 content, aligning with the CODEC-101 fix.

Inside read(byte[], int, int), if the base64 buffer has no data, the method reads raw bytes from the underlying stream and pushes them into the base64 encoder/decoder. Then it returns base64.readResults(...) to emit decoded bytes.

The Base64.readResults(byte[], int, int) method is critical: it returns the number of bytes available in the buffer or -1 if EOF, but returns 0 if no bytes are available and EOF is false.

The problem occurs when the underlying input stream ends exactly on a multiple of 3 bytes. In this case, the base64 buffer is empty (buffer == null), and eof == false (not set), so readResults returns 0 instead of -1 to indicate end of stream. Consequently, Base64InputStream.read(...) returns 0 indicating no bytes read but not EOF, which violates InputStream read contract and breaks InputStreamReader.

This issue was surfaced by "java.io.IOException: Underlying input stream returned zero bytes" from InputStreamReader when wrapping Base64InputStream.

Summary: The root cause is that Base64.readResults() returns 0 (no bytes available, but not EOF) when the underlying stream is exactly a multiple of 3 in length and the buffer is empty. This causes Base64InputStream.read(byte[]) to return 0 instead of -1 at end of stream.

This diagnosis explains the failure seen in the test case. The test data CODEC_101_MULTIPLE_OF_3 has a length multiple of 3, triggering this condition.

The fix should ensure that Base64.readResults treats the end-of-stream condition correctly and never returns 0 when no bytes can be read and EOF is reached. Possibly, the Base64InputStream should detect this condition and return -1 accordingly.

Recent bug reports related to NullPointerException or encoding chunking do not directly relate to this specific zero-byte read issue.

Next steps: Fix locations should be methods Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int) and Base64.readResults(byte[], int, int).

---

Affected methods candidates for fix:
- org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int)
- org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64.readResults(byte[], int, int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int)
Base64.readResults(byte[], int, int)
